Founded by Mamata Banerjee in 1998 as a breakaway faction, this West Bengal party ruled from 2011 until finally losing to the BJP in the 2026 election — which party?
Trinamool Congress: Political party in India.
The last man standing in the Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman founded the Flavian dynasty and was the first emperor to rise from an equestrian family. Who was he?
Vespasian: Roman emperor from AD 69 to 79.
Generally marked by widespread violence and destruction, this armed conflict between states or organized groups is typically waged in pursuit of political, economic, or territorial aims — what is it?
War: Intense armed conflict. It is generally characterized by widespread violence, destruction, and mortality, using regular or irregular military forces.
A descendant of the Viking Rollo and once called 'the Bastard,' this Duke of Normandy won the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and became the first Norman king of England — who was he?
William the Conqueror: King of England from 1066 to 1087.

Born to a family of strawberry farmers in Akita Prefecture, this politician rose to become Japan's Prime Minister from 2020 to 2021 after years as Chief Cabinet Secretary under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Yoshihide Suga: Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021. Yoshihide Suga (菅 義偉, Suga Yoshihide; born 6 December 1948) is a Japanese former politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Franz Reichelt (born 1878) is the earliest of the four. The parachute failed to deploy and he plummeted 57 metres (187 ft) to his death.
Which of these four began earliest?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four.
Perl (founded 1987) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure is a physicist.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Dolph Lundgren is a chemist. Hans "Dolph" Lundgren (Swedish: [ˈdɔlːf ˈlɵ̌nːdɡreːn]; born 3 November 1957) is a Swedish-American actor, filmmaker, and martial artist.
What is the atomic number of Unbiquadium?
Unbiquadium, also known as element 124 or eka-uranium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has placeholder symbol Ubq and atomic number 124.
In what year was David Attenborough born?
David Attenborough: Sir David Frederick Attenborough ( AT-ən-bər-ə; born 8 May 1926) is an English broadcaster, natural historian, and writer.
In what year was Palladium discovered?
Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
In what year was Chromium discovered?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
Mil Mi-28: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.
In which country did the Hawker Hurricane take place?
Hawker Hurricane: United Kingdom. The Air Ministry ordered Hawker's Interceptor Monoplane in late 1934, and the prototype Hurricane K5083 performed its maiden flight on 6 November 1935.
Who is credited with discovering Telescopium?
Telescopium: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is a Latinized form of the Greek word for telescope.
Who is credited with discovering Spontaneous generation?
Spontaneous generation: Anaximander. It was hypothesized that certain forms, such as fleas, could arise from inanimate matter such as dust, or that maggots could arise from dead flesh.
Who is credited with discovering SN 1987A?
SN 1987A: Ian Shelton. SN 1987A was a Type II supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
This Onmyōdō master advised Heian emperors on astrology and spiritual matters; a Kyoto shrine and an Osaka train station now honor him — who is he?
Abe no Seimei (February 21, 921 AD - October 31, 1005) was a Japanese onmyji, a court official and specialist of Onmyd, during the middle of the Heian period.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.

Native to tropical America and carried across the Pacific by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this small tree in the same family as soursop produces a scaly-skinned fruit with sweet, creamy flesh — what's the species?
Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
The second-largest living lizard species after the Komodo dragon, native to South and Southeast Asia. It's a varanid found from India to the Indonesian islands. What is it?
Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
Their foliage is almost indistinguishable from a cycad's, but flower-like reproductive organs — some likely insect-pollinated — set these common Mesozoic seed plants apart. Which extinct order?
Bennettitales (also known as cycadeoids) is an extinct order of seed plants that first appeared in the Permian period and became extinct in most areas toward the end of the Cretaceous.
With the formula B(OH)3 and found in nature as the mineral sassolite, this weak, water-soluble compound of boron serves as an antiseptic, insecticide, and flame retardant — which acid?
Boric acid is a compound of boron, oxygen, and hydrogen with formula B(OH)3.
Atomic number 20 and chemically akin to strontium and barium, this metal is the most common ingredient in limestone — found there as its carbonate. What element?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
A first-generation cephalosporin that can be swallowed rather than infused, this antibiotic disrupts the bacterial cell wall to treat ear, skin and urinary infections — what is it?
Cefalexin is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections. It kills gram-positive and some gram-negative bacteria by disrupting the growth of the bacterial cell wall.
Charted in 1756 by Lacaille and named for the drafting tool that draws circles, this faint southern constellation is easily confused with the mariner's-compass constellation Pyxis. Which one is it?
Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
First created in Germany in 1996 and named for an astronomer on his 537th birthday, this synthetic element (number 112) may even be a gas — which one?
Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
This American biologist, who later ran Caltech and founded the Whitehead Institute, won a Nobel at just 37 for discovering the enzyme reverse transcriptase. Who was he?
David Baltimore (March 7, 1938 - September 6, 2025) was an American biologist, university administrator, and 1975 Nobel laureate in Physiology or Medicine.

Its name comes from a Greek word meaning 'deed' or 'act,' and Aristotle's Poetics contrasted it with the epic and lyric modes; two masks for comedy and tragedy are its emblem. What mode of fiction is it?
Drama is the specific mode of fiction represented in performance: a play, opera, mime, ballet, etc., performed in a theatre, or on radio or television.
This inner lining of the uterus thickens each cycle and is shed during menstruation in humans and a handful of other species, including certain bats and shrews — what is it?
Endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus (womb) in mammals.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.

Found from the tropics to subarctic regions and accounting for about 88% of living amphibian species, this tailless, semiaquatic creature has a name that informally splits into 'toad' for the warty ones — what is it?
Frog is any member of a diverse and largely semiaquatic group of short-bodied, tailless amphibian vertebrates composing the order Anura (coming from the Ancient Greek, literally 'without tail').

Designed at a major tech company in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson, this statically typed, compiled programming language borrows C-like syntax while adding garbage collection and built-in concurrency support — name the language?
Go (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is statically typed and compiled.
About the size of a closed fist and tucked between the lungs, this four-chambered muscular organ pumps blood throughout the body — name it?
Heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
A colourless, ammonia-scented liquid with formula N2H4, this hazardous compound foams polymers, inflates airbags, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Serving as the continuous analog of a summation, this fundamental calculus operation is used to compute areas, volumes, and displacement from velocity — name the mathematical concept?
Integral is the continuous analog of a sum, and is used to calculate areas, volumes, and their generalizations.
Holder of 128 firearm patents, this American engineer invented the telescoping bolt that made compact autoloading pistols possible — who is he?

John Browning (January 23, 1855 - November 26, 1926) was an American firearm designer who developed many varieties of military and civilian firearms, cartridges, and gun mechanisms, many of which are still in use around the world.
This Arab dessert layers spun pastry dough with cheese, soaked in a sugar syrup, with its most famous variant hailing from the Palestinian city of Nablus — what is it?
Knafeh is a traditional Arab dessert made with kadayif (spun pastry dough) layered with cheese and soaked in a sweet, sugar-based syrup called attar.
Found in the support tissues of most plants, this polymer resists rot and reinforces wood and bark structure — what is it?
Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.
This genus of Old World monkeys includes 23 species ranging from Asia and North Africa all the way to Gibraltar, and mostly eats fruit — what is it?
Macaque (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
This small southern-African mongoose has digging foreclaws and a knack for thermoregulating in harsh, dry country, living in tight packs of up to 30 — which sharp-eyed animal is it?
Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
By dividing one cell into two with an identical set of chromosomes apiece, this stage of the cell cycle keeps genetic stability intact across generations — what is it?
Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.
A white crystalline solid built from two fused benzene rings, this aromatic compound is the main ingredient of traditional mothballs and has an odor you can smell at just 0.08 ppm. What is it?
Naphthalene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C10H8.

This biochemical process by which living things use food and water to sustain life can go wrong in either direction, causing malnutrition from either too much or too little of an essential compound — what process is it?
Nutrition is the biochemical and physiological process by which an organism uses food and water to support its life.
This genus of big cats contains the five largest living felines — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — along with extinct relatives like the cave lion — what's the genus called?
Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae.
This flowering plant genus's name traces to a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco, borrowed via French — which South American garden favorite is it?
Petunia is a genus of 20 species of flowering plants of South American origin.
This inflammation of the lining around the lungs causes sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing, and is most often triggered by a viral infection — what condition is it?
Pleurisy is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Barred from a formal education, she learned mathematics from her father's library and wrote to Gauss under the male pseudonym 'Monsieur Le Blanc,' later winning a Paris Academy prize for her work on elasticity. Which French mathematician was she?
Sophie Germain (1 April 1776 - 27 June 1831) was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
This towering perennial grass, native to New Guinea, stores so much natural sweetness in its jointed stalks that it's the world's primary source for a common sweetener — what plant is it?
Sugarcane is a species of tall, perennial grass (in the genus Saccharum, tribe Andropogoneae) that is used for sugar production.
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces the body's hemoglobin production, sometimes causing anemia, an enlarged spleen, and stunted growth in children — what condition is it?
Thalassemia are a group of inherited blood disorders that manifest as the production of reduced hemoglobin.

This androgenic anabolic steroid, part of the nandrolone group, is marketed in ester forms for veterinary use — commonly given to livestock to boost muscle growth and appetite — what's the steroid called?
Trenbolone is an androgen and anabolic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group which itself was never marketed for human use.
This southwestern European viper's bite can be more dangerous than the common adder's — up to 4% of untreated cases are fatal — which species?
Vipera aspis is a viper species found in southwestern Europe.

This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under PM Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for opposing EU-imposed austerity, before co-founding the left-wing party DiEM25 — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis (born 24 March 1961) is a Greek economist, academic, author, and politician.

Nicknamed wolfsbane, monkshood, and devil's helmet, this highly toxic genus of over 250 mountain-dwelling flowering plants thrives in moist, well-draining soils across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Aconitum: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
Which Swiss chemist was the first person to synthesize and personally experience the effects of LSD, later isolating the active compounds in magic mushrooms?
Named for its males' mating call, which sounds like a farm animal bellowing, this large amphibian native to eastern North America has been introduced worldwide as a food source — which species?
American bullfrog: Species of amphibian. It typically inhabits large permanent water bodies such as swamps, ponds, and lakes.
Evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the Cretaceous, these insects are easily spotted by their elbowed antennae and slender, node-waisted bodies — what are they?
Ant: Family of insects. Nearly all ant colonies also have some fertile males called "drones" and one or more fertile females called "queens" (gynes).
Sold under the brand name Abilify, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and irritability linked to autism spectrum disorder — what is it?
Aripiprazole: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Aripiprazole is taken by mouth or via injection into a muscle.
Evolving from a troubled twin-engine predecessor into a four-engine heavy bomber powered by Rolls-Royce Merlin engines, which British WWII aircraft became one of the RAF's most famous bombers?
Avro Lancaster: World War II British heavy bomber aircraft.
Nicknamed 'top shelf' dizziness, this inner-ear disorder causes brief spinning sensations lasting under a minute whenever you tilt or turn your head — what is this condition called?
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: Medical condition. Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), sometimes called "top shelf vertigo", is a disorder arising from a problem in the inner ear.

In this distributed ledger, each record holds a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering a single block would require rewriting every block that follows — making the data nearly tamper-proof. What is it?
Blockchain: Distributed data store for digital transactions.

Originating from feral Eastern Mediterranean populations, this single wild plant species has been cultivated into an astonishing range of vegetables including broccoli, cauliflower, kale, and Brussels sprouts. What is it?
Brassica oleracea: Species of plant. Brassica oleracea, also known as wild cabbage in its uncultivated form, is a plant of the family Brassicaceae.

Ranging from the hefty black species of the Amazon basin to the diminutive dwarf species just over a metre long, these Central and South American relatives of alligators make up their own reptile subfamily — what are they called?
Caiman: Subfamily of reptiles. The black caiman is the largest caiman species in the world and is found in the slow-moving rivers and lakes that surround the Amazon basin.

Born in London, raised in Milan, and self-taught in web design, this Catholic teenager built a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles before dying of leukemia at fifteen — he was beatified in 2020. Who was he?
Which second-generation antihistamine for hay fever kicks in within half an hour but is more likely than fexofenadine or loratadine to cause drowsiness?

Cetirizine: Antihistamine medication. Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
This plant genus includes both chicory, whose roasted roots make a coffee substitute, and true endive, the base for salad greens like escarole — which genus?
Cichorium: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Named for an Indonesian island where an 18th-century naturalist first catalogued it, this pungent, oregano-scented succulent also goes by Cuban oregano and Indian borage — which plant?
Coleus amboinicus: Species of plant. Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.
This mostly inactive steroid hormone is created when an enzyme shields organs like the kidneys by converting active cortisol into its inactive form — what is it?
Cortisone: Corticosteroid precursor and metabolite of cortisol.
Started in 1955 by an army colonel and a cynologist as an experiment, this hybrid dog breed became officially recognized as a national breed in 1982 — which one?
Czechoslovakian Wolfdog: Czech and Slovak breed of dog.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
This Eastern Han hydrologist is credited as the first to harness a waterwheel to power the bellows of a blast furnace for forging cast iron — who was this ingenious engineer?
Du Shi: 1st-century engineer, metallurgist and politician.
This Hungarian nuclear chemist became the world's leading expert in isotope separation and polonium preparation, and confirmed the existence of "Uranium-Y" — who was she?
This class of chemical compound forms when an acid's hydroxyl hydrogen is swapped for an organic group, and includes the glycerides that make up most animal fats — what is it?
Ester: Compound derived from an acid.

Recognized by their pod-like fruit and compound leaves, this plant family — the third-largest among flowering plants — includes beans, peas, and lentils along with genera like Acacia and Mimosa. What family is it?
Fabaceae: Family of legume flowering plants. Fabaceae or Leguminosae, commonly known as the legume, pea, or bean family, is a large and agriculturally important family of flowering plants.
This whip-like appendage propels sperm cells and lets bacteria like Helicobacter pylori swim through stomach mucus, sometimes triggering ulcers — what is it called?
Flagellum: Cellular appendage functioning as locomotive or sensory organelle.
Sold under the brand name Lasix, this loop diuretic treats edema from heart failure and kidney disease and can also cause tinnitus and light sensitivity?

Furosemide: Loop diuretic medication. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
Caught from contaminated water and common among travelers and children, this parasitic infection causes fatty, sticky diarrhea weeks after exposure — what is it?
Giardiasis: Parasitic disease that results in diarrhea.
With a black head, white cheeks and yellow underparts, this widespread European songbird was split from two Asian relatives after 2005 DNA studies?
Great tit: Passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

Nicknamed the 'Halloween beetle' in North America for invading homes each October to overwinter, this extremely color-variable insect was introduced there from eastern Asia to control aphids — what species is it?
Harmonia axyridis: Species of beetle. Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.
Known scientifically as singultus, this involuntary diaphragm spasm closes the glottis in about 35 milliseconds to produce a signature sound — what reflex is it?
Hiccup: Involuntary contraction of the diaphragm. The rhythm of the hiccup, or the time between hiccups, tends to be relatively constant.

Made of one oxygen and one hydrogen atom bonded together with a negative charge, this ion is the active base in the sodium compound used to produce millions of tons of industrial chemicals yearly. What ion is it?
Expressed with symbols like < and >, this relation shows that one quantity is less than or greater than another, rather than equal — what's it called?
Inequality (mathematics): Mathematical relation making a non-equal comparison.

His 1962 book The Calculus of Consent launched a theory of how politicians' and bureaucrats' self-interest shapes their decisions, earning him the 1986 Nobel in economics — which founder of public choice theory is this?
James M. Buchanan: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1919–2013)
This British-American designer ran industrial design at Apple alongside Steve Jobs, then founded the creative collective LoveFrom working with Ferrari and OpenAI — who is he?
First described in 1816 and classified as an impulse-control disorder, this is the inability to resist stealing things you don't even need — what's it called?
Kleptomania: Inability to resist the urge to steal.
Formulated in 1834, this principle of electromagnetism states that an induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the very change in magnetic field that created it — which principle?
Lenz's law: Electromagnetic opposition to change.

Providing the USAF with intercontinental strategic airlift for oversized cargo, this jumbo transport is among the largest military aircraft ever built and shares lineage with the smaller Starlifter — what is it?
Lockheed C-5 Galaxy: American heavy military transport aircraft.
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, and the quokka among its 63 recognized species — what is it?
Macropodidae: Family of marsupial mammals. Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.

Captured by Einstein's famous equation E=mc², this principle shows that a tiny amount of one physical quantity converts into an enormous amount of another thanks to the speed of light being squared — what is this relationship called?
Mass–energy equivalence: Physics concept expressed as E = mc².
Aristotle called it the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes existence itself, what all things have in common, and how reality is divided into categories of being. Which field is it?
Cultivated by the Aztecs and named partly for a Mexican state capital, this flower opens each evening between four and eight o'clock and perfumes the night before closing by morning — which plant?

Mirabilis jalapa: Species of flower. Mirabilis jalapa, the marvel of Peru or four o'clock flower, is the most commonly grown ornamental species of Mirabilis plant, and is available in a range of colors.
Serving as Turkey's minister overseeing environment and climate, who is set to preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31?
A healthy kidney contains up to 1.5 million of these microscopic filtering units, each pairing a capillary tuft with a cup-shaped capsule — what is it called?
Nephron: Microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Built from a nitrogen-containing base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, these molecules are the monomer building blocks of DNA and RNA — what are they called?
Nucleotide: Biological molecules constituting nucleic acids.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this degenerative joint disease comes from the breakdown of cartilage and bone, often striking the fingertips, thumb base, knees, and hips — what is it?
Osteoarthritis: Form of arthritis caused by degeneration of joints.
Known as the passion flower, this genus of about 550 species also has ornamental hybrids that have won Royal Horticultural Society awards and varieties used in ayahuasca analogs — name the genus?
Passiflora: Genus of flowering plants in the passion flower family.
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

A member of the cashew family, this tree nut is a priority allergen, yet the world still churned out 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — with the US, Iran, and Turkey making up 87% of it. Which green-hued nut is it?
Pistachio: Member of the cashew family. The pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.
This imperial unit of pressure equals about 6.895 kilopascals and is the number you check when filling a bicycle tire to around 65 — which unit?
Pound per square inch: Unit of pressure or stress. It is the pressure resulting from a force with magnitude of one pound-force applied to an area of one square inch.

Covering the asymmetric relationship between citizens and the state — including constitutional, administrative, tax, and criminal matters — this branch of the legal system contrasts with the branch governing relationships between individuals — which branch?
Public law: Law governing government actions.
One of the oldest groups of eukaryotic seaweed, this phylum boasts over 7,000 species — mostly marine, though about 5% live in freshwater habitats. What group is it?
Red algae: Division of plant life.

Also called black locust or false acacia, this deciduous legume-family tree is native to just a few small pockets of the United States but has been planted so widely it's now considered invasive elsewhere — which tree?
Robinia pseudoacacia: Species of tree native to North America.
Containing the potent compound salvinorin A, this plant used by Mazatec shamans for spiritual healing sparked a US media panic around 2007 after being shared in online videos — which plant?
Salvia divinorum: Species of plant. The leaves contain the potent compound salvinorin A and can induce a dissociative state and hallucinations.
Located between the bladder and the rectum in male mammals, this paired accessory gland produces most of the fluid released during ejaculation — what is it?
Seminal vesicles: Pair of simple tubular glands.

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.
A competitive physical activity that maintains or improves physical ability and skills, this can involve teams or individuals and may be open to broad participation or restricted. What is this?
Sport: Forms of competitive activity, usually physical.
This bright yellow nonmetal — element 16, known since ancient times in India, Greece and China — forms cyclic eight-atom rings under normal conditions. What is it?
Sulfur: Chemical element with atomic number 16 (S)
Every part of this evergreen tree is poisonous except its fleshy red aril, yet its wood was long prized for making longbows and lutes. What species, often planted in churchyards, is it?
Taxus baccata: Species of conifer in the family Taxaceae.
Commonly nicknamed 'tree of life' from Latin, this genus of coniferous evergreens in the cypress family includes species native to both North America and eastern Asia. What's the genus?
Thuja: Genus of conifers. Thuja ( THEW-yə) is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
Patented in 1956, this glucocorticoid treats skin conditions, allergies, and rheumatic disorders, and was the 108th most prescribed U.S. medication in 2023 — which drug?
Triamcinolone: Steroid medication. Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Home to Polaris, the North Star, this far-northern constellation is also nicknamed the Little Dipper — which one?
Ursa Minor: Constellation in the northern celestial hemisphere.
This German experimental physicist shared the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physics with Max Born for the 'coincidence method' — the circuitry he used to study the Compton effect and cosmic rays. Who was he?
Nicknamed 'birch sugar' because it can be extracted from birch wood, this crystalline sugar substitute is chemically classified as an alditol — what is it?
The symbol for potassium is K. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K and atomic number 19.
What is the chemical symbol for erbium?
The symbol for erbium is Er. Erbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Er and atomic number 68.
